input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

seventeenth of April, at nine twenty in the morning to handle the exchange for the two seats on the Harbor Line from Bellwether to Grayhaven. The original booking is under Leah Morris, and the reference is NC74291. The train leaves at eleven ten and reaches Grayhaven at one thirty-five. The exchange concerns the outward journey only, and Leah is keeping the return ticket for Sunday evening. Her brother Daniel is coming with her to the counter because he has the payment card and the booking email on his phone.

The station office is beside platform three near the old brass clock, and its public counter opens at eight forty-five on Thursday. Leah plans to bring the printed confirmation as well as her rail discount card. The confirmation shows seats twenty-one and twenty-two in coach B and a total fare of sixty-eight pounds forty pence. She wants to exchange them for the nine forty service if there are two seats together and if the exchange fee is no more than twelve pounds in total. If either condition is not met, she will keep the eleven ten train and ask about another date instead. Daniel has asked the clerk to explain any fare difference before making the exchange.

Leah said, “Please check the nine forty train first because I have to be at the Harbor Clinic before eleven, and the earlier arrival gives me time to walk from the station.” She also said the clinic appointment is at ten thirty and that the entrance is on Ferry Street rather than the main road. Daniel replied, “We can take the number six bus if it is raining, but we should leave enough time to find the stop.” The forecast in their message says light rain is possible between eight and ten, but it does not give a probability. Leah has not decided whether to use the bus.

The ticket exchange has three details the clerk needs to check:
1. The two tickets must stay on the same booking, and both passengers must travel together.
2. The new seats should be together if that is available on the nine forty service.
3. Leah wants the return ticket left unchanged, and Daniel wants a printed receipt for the card payment.

The booking email includes a note that the discount card expires in June, but it is still valid on the date of travel. The clerk may ask to see it before calculating the difference.

Daniel will keep the phone charged and save a screenshot of the booking reference in case the station connection is slow. He has also written the train times on a small blue envelope with the appointment address and the clinic phone number inside it. The envelope is in the front pocket of Leah's brown bag. She will carry the discount card in her wallet and the printed confirmation in a clear sleeve so the ink does not get wet if it rains. Neither of them has asked the clinic to change the appointment, and they are not assuming that the earlier train will have seats available.

If the clerk confirms that two seats together are available and that the total exchange fee is twelve pounds or less, Leah will ask the clerk to exchange the outward tickets for the nine forty service before paying. Daniel will check the new departure and arrival times on the printed receipt. If the clerk says the seats are separate or the fee is more than twelve pounds, they will not make that exchange at the counter. Leah will keep the current tickets and ask whether the same conditions could be checked for the following Thursday. This condition matters because the clinic said the appointment can be moved only if Leah calls before five o'clock on Thursday, and she has not yet made that call.

At the office, Daniel will show the booking email and the card while Leah explains that only the outward journey is being considered. They will listen for the clerk to state the full fee and the seat numbers before any payment is made. Leah has placed a reminder on her phone for eight fifteen so they can leave the apartment with time to walk to the station and wait for the counter to open. If they need to use the ticket machine for a platform update, they can do that after speaking with the clerk. The original eleven ten departure remains on their confirmation unless the exchange is completed, and neither of them has received a message saying that the booking has already changed.

After the counter visit, Leah will text her neighbor Iris to say whether she is still leaving at eleven ten or is planning around the nine forty train. She will not promise an arrival time at the clinic until she has the printed details. Daniel will take the receipt home and put it with the Sunday return ticket paperwork. The two of them have agreed to keep the blue envelope until the journey is finished because it has the clinic address and the station information together. Leah said, “I want the outward trip sorted out, but I still need to see the fee and the seats before I decide.” The appointment, the return ticket, and the current booking reference remain separate details even if the clerk can complete the exchange on Thursday."}]
